title: Finite-ring bounded lisse complexes and finite derived isomorphism sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] use $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finite $B$-module stalks, there is an etale covering on which $K$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf complex associated to a bounded complex of finite $B$-modules. For two such complexes $K,L$, the sheafification on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(K|_V,L|_V)$ is finite locally constant; locally on constant models $E,G$ its fibre is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. The analogous sheaf of isomorphisms is finite locally constant, possibly empty. On a connected $X$, for any geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $K$ is etale locally isomorphic to the constant complex $K_{\bar x}$. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant. Agent extension of Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, from perfect source to bounded finite source and bounded target by a finite free approximation; finite derived Hom and connected constancy are agent arguments

proof.text: Prove the strengthened local-model assertion by induction on $b-a$: for every $a\leq b$ and every input supported cohomologically in $[a,b]$, there is an etale cover on which it is the constant complex of finite $B$-modules concentrated in $[a,b]$. The standard t-structure supplies a representative zero above $b$. Replace its degree-$a$ term by the cokernel of the incoming differential and its terms below $a$ by zero. The outgoing differential descends since $d^a d^{a-1}=0$; cycles modulo boundaries are unchanged at and above $a$, and below $a$ both old cohomology and new terms are zero. This gives a quasi-isomorphic representative $A^\bullet$ with terms zero outside $[a,b]$. For $a=b$, the map to $H^a(K)[-a]$ is a quasi-isomorphism; trivialize this locally constant sheaf. Its constant value is finite because it is its stalk at any geometric point of the nonempty cover member. Empty members can be discarded; if $X$ is empty use the empty cover. For $K=0$ take the zero model.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: For $a<b$, trivialize $H^b(K)=\underline M$ and choose a surjection $B^r\to M$ (a finite module over a finite ring has a finite generating set). Since $A^{b+1}=0$, the quotient $A^b\to H^b(A)$ is an epimorphism of sheaves. Apply the finite-free local lifting lemma to the composite $\underline{B^r}\to\underline M=H^b(A)$. Its local lift to $A^b$ is a chain map $\underline{B^r}[-b]\to A^\bullet$, as the outgoing differential is zero. Thus no lifting of hypercohomology classes is assumed. Complete this map to a triangle $\underline{B^r}[-b]\to K\to L\to\underline{B^r}[-b+1]$. Its cohomology sequence gives $H^i(L)=H^i(K)$ for $i\leq b-2$, zero above $b-1$, and $0\to H^{b-1}(K)\to H^{b-1}(L)\to\underline{\ker(B^r\to M)}\to0$. The constant kernel identity follows from exactness of constant finite-module sequences; the Serre lemma makes $H^{b-1}(L)$ finite locally constant. All $H^i(L)$ therefore satisfy the induction hypotheses on $[a,b-1]$.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to $L$, obtaining $\underline{M^\bullet}$ in $[a,b-1]$. The connecting map $\delta:L\to\underline{B^r}[-b+1]$ factors through $H^{b-1}(L)[-b+1]$: in the standard truncation triangle its restriction to $\tau_{\leq b-2}L$ is zero by orthogonality, so Hom-out-of-triangle exactness supplies the factorization. Shift both single-degree objects by $b-1$ and apply the connective-single-Hom theorem with a target in degree zero; it identifies the resulting derived map with an ordinary sheaf map $H^{b-1}(L)\to\underline{B^r}$. Compose with $\underline{M^{b-1}}\to H^{b-1}(L)$. By the constant-sheaf morphism lemma, after a further cover this composite is a $B$-linear map $t:M^{b-1}\to B^r$. It kills the image of $d^{b-2}$, since it factors through cohomology; equality is checked on a geometric stalk of each nonempty member. Thus $M^a\to\cdots\to M^{b-1}\xrightarrow{-t}B^r$ is a complex in $[a,b]$. This is the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]$ after dropping its zero summands: shifting the cone changes the off-diagonal differential to $-t$, while keeping the differential of $M^\bullet$. Rotation gives a triangle $\underline{B^r}[-b]\to\underline{\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]}\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}\underline{B^r}[-b+1]$. Compare it to the preceding triangle by TR3 with identities on $L$ and $\underline{B^r}[-b+1]$. The long-exact cohomology sequences give an isomorphism on the remaining term (injectivity and surjectivity follow by chasing the two neighboring identity maps); the comparison is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, hence invertible in the localization. This identifies the constructed complex with $K$. This completes the induction and the first clause.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Apply the proved local-model assertion separately to $K$ and $L$. Refine by $U_i\times_X W_j$: these are etale over $X$ and jointly surjective because each of the two families is. On each member write the restrictions as $\underline E$ and $\underline G$, with $E,G$ bounded finite-module complexes. For every bounded finite-free complex $F$ and chain map $F\to E$, each cone term $F^{i+1}\oplus E^i$ is a finite set, so its cohomology is finite (a quotient of a subgroup). The finite-cone free-model theorem applies over $B$ and produces a quasi-isomorphism $P\to E$ with finite-free terms and $P^i=0$ above an upper bound $e$ for $E$. This invokes its statement, not its construction, and does not assert that $E$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Choose $g$ with $G^i=0$ for $i<g$, and $m\leq\min(e,g-2)$. Put $F=\sigma_{\geq m}P$, the finite complex keeping $P^i$ for $m\leq i\leq e$ and zero elsewhere. The inclusion $F\to P$ is an isomorphism on cohomology for $i>m$ and surjective for $i=m$, by the cycles/boundaries formula. Thus the cone $C$ of $F\to E$ has cohomology zero in degrees $i\geq m$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(C[-1],G)=0$, since $C\in D^{\leq m-1}$ and $C[-1]\in D^{\leq m}$ whereas $G\in D^{\geq g}$. Hom-out-of-triangle exactness, using rotations of $F\to E\to C$, gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$. The identical calculation applies on every localized etale site after taking constant sheaves: exactness of constant finite-module sequences identifies cohomology of the constant cone with the constant cohomology of $C$. These identifications commute with restriction because they are all induced by precomposition with the one fixed map $F\to E$.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Compute the sheafified Hom from $\underline F$ to $\underline G$. By the local-actual lemma (1), every derived morphism is locally a chain map. Apply the constant-sheaf morphism lemma to its finitely many components: on a common refinement each is a $B$-linear map $F^i\to G^i$. Their chain equations hold in $B$-modules because constant module maps are detected at a geometric stalk on every nonempty member. This proves local surjectivity of the map from the constant presheaf with value the chain maps modulo homotopy to the derived Hom presheaf. For local injectivity, subtract two algebraic representatives with equal image in actual derived Hom; their difference is locally null-homotopic by local-actual (2). Apply the constant-sheaf morphism lemma to the finitely many $h^i:F^i\to G^{i-1}$ of the homotopy; at a geometric stalk their equations $\alpha^i=d_Gh^i+h^{i+1}d_F^i$ become the same equations of modules, so the algebraic homotopy class is zero. The bounded-projective derived-map-representative theorem identifies these algebraic homotopy classes with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$. There are only finitely many degreewise maps (all $F^i,G^i$ are finite and only finitely many occur), hence finitely many chain maps and homotopy classes. Together with the preceding step this identifies the Hom sheaf for $\underline E,\underline G$ with the constant finite set $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. All maps are induced by constant coefficient maps and restriction, so these local descriptions prove finite local constancy for the original $K,L$. The site sheafification-sections lemma now proves the resulting map of sheaves is bijective: locally represent a target section by an actual presheaf morphism, use the proved local surjectivity, and glue the preimages, which agree locally on overlaps by local injectivity. Local injectivity also proves uniqueness of this glued section. This uses the lemma for presheaves of sets in a universe containing the site, not an unproved property of the universal-property definition of sheafification.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Under the Hom-sheaf identification, the sheafification of the isomorphism presheaf is the constant subset $\operatorname{Isom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. Indeed an algebraic isomorphism and its inverse give inverse constant derived maps. Conversely, if a constant algebraic map represents an actual derived isomorphism on a nonempty etale object, an exact geometric stalk functor takes its inverse to an inverse in $D(B)$, so the map was an algebraic isomorphism. A germ coming from a sheafified isomorphism can be represented by an actual isomorphism after a cover by the site sheafification-sections lemma. Equalities with the local constant Hom representative can be made actual after a further cover, so the preceding test applies to germs as well. On overlaps the algebraic isomorphism representatives agree after refinement by the local injectivity proved for Hom; the same site-sections lemma then glues them to the constant isomorphism sheaf, with uniqueness. Hence the isomorphism sheaf is finite locally constant; its value is the empty set when the two model objects are not isomorphic. Exactness and the constant-stalk theorem are used on underlying abelian groups, and their naturality with multiplication by every $b\in B$ makes the same maps $B$-linear.

proof.text: Suppose $X$ is connected and $\bar x$ is a geometric point, and set $E_0=K_{\bar x}$. For each local model $\underline E_j$ on a nonempty cover member $U_j$, exact stalks and the constant-stalk identification give $K_{\bar y}\simeq E_j$ for every geometric point of $U_j$. Define $O\subseteq X$ as the union of the images of those members whose model is isomorphic in $D(B)$ to $E_0$. These images are open because etale morphisms are open. The complement is the union of the images of the other members: an overlap would give a geometric point and identify their two fibres, contradicting the different isomorphism classes. Thus $O$ is both open and closed and contains $x$. Connectedness forces $O=X$. Every nonempty member therefore has $E_j\simeq E_0$, and composing this algebraic isomorphism with its local-model isomorphism gives an etale covering trivializing $K$ as $\underline{K_{\bar x}}$. This proves the connected clause globally, not only near $\bar x$. No step used a finite Tor bound. The empty scheme has no geometric point, so this clause is vacuous.
